summary.oneLiner:
AvenuesAI (ex-Infibeam Avenues) re-badged itself this quarter from a payment gateway into an "AI-first
financial infrastructure and transaction intelligence platform," and FY26 headline growth is spectacular
only at the gross line — revenue from operations **+103% to ₹8,116cr** while **net revenue rose just +15%
to ₹603cr**, i.e. the growth is TPV pass-through, not monetisation. The real Q4 news is strategic, not
financial: a declared asset-light pivot into embedded lending via **minority NBFC stakes** (Ratnaafin, up to
2.5%) and a **proposed strategic investment in Online PSB Loans announced on the call day**, plus a
**confidential DRHP filed for Rediff**. Management explicitly withheld FY27 guidance ("we'll give guidance in
the first quarter call for the full year"), pre-empted a profit re-rating ("we don't see a hockey stick in
FY '27 in profitability"), and — unusually — conceded its prior AI/US thesis was mistimed: "yes, we were
wrong in terms of thinking that AI adoption in such large financial enterprises will become much cleaner,
faster."

guidance (critical — verify next quarter: FY27 guidance was explicitly DEFERRED, not given: "But we'll give guidance in the first quarter call
for the full year." Repeated for margins: "which will guide you at the end of first quarter."
→ The Q1 FY27 call is where FY27 guidance lands. That call has already occurred relative to the
processing date — this note's guidance section is therefore stale on arrival and must be checked against
the Q1 FY27 disclosure.
Revenue growth: no number. Qualitatively, FY27 framed as the year the building blocks compound —
"FY '27, in our view, becomes a year where scale, intelligence, monetization, lending, AI orchestration,
international expansion and ecosystem integration, they begin reinforcing one another more visibly."
Profitability — actively damped: "we don't see a hockey stick in FY '27 in profitability" and
"it's reasonable to assume that it will be similar to what we have seen in the past years FY '27 should
be." Operating leverage conceded only "in pockets".
Margin: "in terms of consolidated basis, we should continue seeing similar numbers or maybe slightly
higher" — against an acknowledged headwind: "we are in the payment gateway business is somewhat — there
is margin pressure."
Take rates — deliberately not optimised: "our focus remains on building long-term ecosystem value
rather than optimizing for short-term take rates", but also "We'll work very hard in terms of ensuring
that we are able to get our take rates better, and that will require quite a bit of work and optimization."
Capex / commissioning dates: refused. "in terms of the capex, we have certain guidelines and
policies that we are not able to share a lot of information about, specifics on Rediff." No capex number,
no NBFC-investment quantum beyond the 2.5% Ratnaafin stake, no commissioning dates of any kind.
Platform segment: "you will see a lot more activities on the platform side in FY '27" and
"you'll see some amount of growth in that business" — undated, unquantified.
AI revenue: "We do have specific AI revenue as well, which from a size of the P&L is not material" →
"as and when it becomes large enough that we'd want to talk about it, and you'll hear more and more of
that in this year from us."
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business; no backlog, inflow or pipeline metric is reported. The nearest equivalents
disclosed on the call are merchant-acquisition proxies, all volume-based and unmonetised in the disclosure:
Form builder: "more than 5,000 merchants were onboarded on the form builder in less than a month" —
serving "a lot of education institutions, a lot of small merchants, a lot of event merchants."
Hospitality vertical: "now we're scaling up to more than 3,000 hotels, where we're building the entire
central reservation system along with the payment gateway built in" — certified with Opera and
Micros-Fidelio, "which is used by almost all the 5-stars and some of the bigger 4-star chains",
integrating to GDS/PMS so bookings from "any OTA like Booking.com or Expedia or MakeMyTrip" settle
automatically.
Q4 merchant wins: "there has been a good merchant wins that we have had in this last Q4 quarter, which
has translated into good growth of TPV"; strength in "utility, government payments, B2B payments."
Share-of-wallet capture (a cost, admitted): "merchants will be using multiple payment options —
payment gateway options. And we have been very consciously going after the merchants to move processing
volumes to us. It comes at a cost, but I think it's one worth making."
segment / subsidiary detail: Payments — CCAvenue (the engine). Enterprise merchant acquiring across enterprises, SMEs, education,
travel, telecom, government and digital commerce. Growth driver stated as platform-plus-payments, not
gateway pricing: "you put up a platform layer over a payments layer, so it becomes a big hook for bigger
merchants to stay on and increase volumes… It's just another vanilla payment gateway. So it's a platform
plus payments play that has come."
Platform / e-commerce software — flat, and it is the high-margin line. The analyst framing was
"your e-commerce platform is kind of degrowing… that's a high-margin business for us." Management
corrected the direction but not the substance: "the platform business is slightly flat to slightly
higher… the full year numbers in the segment there, you'll see that they are somewhat flat to slightly
higher." Fix proposed is FY27 product rebuild + international.
Rediff / RediffOne / RediffPay — being repositioned from media to fintech. "Historically, Rediff was
viewed primarily as an Internet media and communication platform. We increasingly see it becoming a
broader consumer engagement and financial participation layer", expanding "into areas including payments,
financial engagement, wealth, participation in brokerage, consumer commerce." RediffPay is a
consumer-facing UPI app — "It's actually live and in production", currently being stabilised then
scaled. Today "most of the business is B2B." Rediff has filed a confidential DRHP — "Given the
regulatory compliances, we are not able to share anything additional at this time."
XDuce (US, 20% associate). Taken 2024, $10 million for 20% — "we have not acquired. We've taken
20% in XDuce." Profitable: "they have been a profitable company. They make a few million dollars every
year." Governance stance stated flatly: "We don't participate in the Board of XDuce and we don't allocate
the funds. They have their own control mechanism." (See §10 — this was the sharpest exchange on the call.)
International. FY26 focus was Middle East + GIFT City. FY27 pivots to the US: "This year, we will pick
up U.S. because of the macroeconomic risk in Middle East" — and the internal doctrine, verbatim:
"where we think that we have lighted a small fire, we pour gasoline on it until it becomes larger."
Embedded finance / NBFC stakes. "We are not going to put our balance sheet for lending… What we will
do selectively is to invest minority stakes in more than one NBFC." First is Ratnaafin — "up to
2.5%". Screen for further stakes: "NBFCs with a few thousand crores of AUM, which have a good operating
history, which have scale, which are next generation and well-run management." Plus the Online PSB
Loans proposed strategic investment — "potentially connects us to one of India's most important digital
lending infrastructure backed by major financial institutions."
AI stack. IAIRO (India AI Research Organization) participation, CommerceAI, PayCentral, agent
frameworks across "transaction routing, merchant operations, fraud management, reconciliation, compliance,
automation and customer engagement."
growth verticals / optionality: Agentic payments — the most concrete new capability described. "we have bit of payment agents as well,
just to let you know." Architecture given end-to-end: a discovery agent finds the option, customer
intent converts it to a command, then "that execution will go from discovery agent to a payment agent. So
there will be an agent to agent protocol transfer that happens. And that payment agent is actually
going to go again to AvenuesAI's payment framework, whether it's through MCP… or it will go directly
into executing that if the merchant is integrated using CCAvenue." Two-factor auth remains the human gate.
Embedded merchant lending — merchant financing, checkout financing, working capital, consumer
financing, AI-assisted underwriting, distributed through NBFC partners, no own balance sheet.
Rediff IPO — confidential DRHP filed; an analyst explicitly raised the SOTP angle: "maybe there
will be an SOPP kind of valuation, which might emerge if and when we get Rediff listed."
Sovereign-data-stack pull — "given the macroeconomics of data, data privacy and sovereignty of data,
there's a lot of incentives for very large institutions and merchants to move to a sovereign stack… we
believe it becomes a very large opportunity in '27 and '28."
US cross-border acquiring — "cross-border commerce, global merchant acquiring international
settlements and AI-native payment orchestration represents a large underpenetrated opportunity."
Direct AI revenue — exists, "from a size of the P&L is not material", framed as future optionality.
6a. moat & competitive position: Workflow lock-in beats gateway pricing — evidenced with named certifications. The hospitality build is
a full central reservation system certified with Opera / Micros-Fidelio, integrated to GDS and property
management systems so that "when reservation comes in through, say, any OTA like Booking.com or Expedia or
MakeMyTrip, it gets automated systems and payments are collected automatically." Management's own
conclusion: "those workloads customization is where we are winning, putting a platform with a payments
play. That's where the real growth for us is coming." Scale evidence: 3,000+ hotels.
Distribution velocity on self-serve tooling: "more than 5,000 merchants were onboarded on the form
builder in less than a month."
Data/intelligence compounding — asserted, not yet evidenced with a metric: "The more transactions we
process, the more intelligent the platform accumulates… the stronger the long-term defensibility of the
platform." Recorded as management's stated moat thesis; no supporting number was offered, so treat as
claim rather than demonstrated moat.
Where they explicitly disclaim a moat: compute. "we don't have a very large role to play in compute
because we're not a chip design firm, we don't manufacture chips and we are not going that route. So we
just think that we have to work on algos and data."
margins & cost dynamics: Core gateway margin is under pressure, stated plainly: "We are in the payment gateway business is
somewhat — there is margin pressure."
Costs are front-loaded and deliberate: "Quite a few of other costs are front loaded, specifically some
of the investments that we're making in the AI setup and also, the opportunities that are there in front of
us."
Operating leverage is partial: "in pockets, we are seeing the operating leverage kicking in with
scale", aided by "the productivity that we are getting through this optimization and productivity gains
from AI are also not insignificant."
Winning share costs money: moving merchant volume off competing gateways "comes at a cost."
The mix problem: the high-margin platform line is flat while the low-margin gross-payment line more than
doubled — mathematically a mix headwind to the net-revenue margin, even though management guides
consolidated margin to "similar numbers or maybe slightly higher."
AI is a cost today, revenue tomorrow: direct AI revenue is "not material" to the P&L while AI
infrastructure spend is explicitly part of the front-loaded cost base.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): No capex number was given, and the refusal was explicit when asked directly for capex guidance across
NBFC investments, infrastructure and Rediff: "in terms of the capex, we have certain guidelines and
policies that we are not able to share a lot of information about, specifics on Rediff."
Capex philosophy, in their framing: "more at a capex level, we look at three things, which is in the
world of AI, genuinely, we think there's only compute, algos and data" — with compute explicitly
excluded from their remit.
Committed / announced deployments (amounts mostly undisclosed): Ratnaafin NBFC minority up to 2.5%;
Online PSB Loans proposed strategic investment (quantum not disclosed); XDuce $10mn for 20% (2024,
historic); Rediff platform investment (quantum withheld); US market build-out (undated, unquantified);
AI infrastructure (part of the front-loaded cost base, unquantified).
Discipline claim: "Our strategy is not subsidiary-led growth. Our strategy is infrastructure-led,
intelligence-led and ecosystem-led growth."
⚠️ Slippage watch: the US expansion is itself an admitted slip — the 30% international revenue
target was set in February 2024 and, per the analyst and undisputed by management, "as of now, also, we
are not close to that number." Track the US build and the international mix against that original target.
capital allocation: Explicit refusal to become a lender: "We are not going to put our balance sheet for lending."
Restated by Vishwas Patel: "our strategy remains asset-light and scalable. We are not looking to become a
traditional balance sheet lender."
Chosen instrument: repeated small minority stakes in NBFCs, deliberately more than one —
"invest minority stakes in more than one NBFC"; Ratnaafin is "the first one that we've opened up, where
we've taken up, up to 2.5%." Rationale is ecosystem access, not returns on the stake: "we are able to
connect our ecosystem very tightly with such NBFCs… and we would allow the NBFCs to continue opening up the
lending opportunities to our merchant and merchant ecosystem and consumer ecosystems."
Online PSB Loans — proposed strategic investment announced on the call day, positioned as access to
"one of India's most important digital lending infrastructure backed by major financial institutions."
Rediff monetisation via IPO — confidential DRHP filed; details withheld under regulatory silence.
XDuce — capital allocated, control expressly not retained. This is the governance question of the call
(§10): AvenuesAI put $10mn into a 20% stake and states "We don't participate in the Board of XDuce and we
don't allocate the funds."
No dividend, buyback, debt-reduction, promoter-pledge or fund-raise discussion occurred on this call.
risks & watch-items: 1. The XDuce capital-deployment challenge — the sharpest exchange on the call. Analyst Ayushi:
"when we acquired XDuce, the Board had stated two specific objectives. One was that we were embedding
Phronetic AI into XDuce's framework, and then second was growing CCAvenue's U.S. payment business. So
since that investment, XDuce has made at least two significant capital deployments that are entirely
unrelated to those objectives" — specifically "one investment in a U.S. cybersecurity firm and the other
investment in DEV Information Technologies, which is an Indian listed company… they have spent around
INR12 crores in that particular transaction." Management's reply was a governance disclaimer, not a
rebuttal on substance: "I think that's an incorrect statement. We don't participate in the Board of XDuce
and we don't allocate the funds." Watch: whether the two stated XDuce objectives are ever delivered.
2. A multi-year target publicly missed. "the 30% target for international revenue was made in February
2024. Sir, as of now, also, we are not close to that number. So what do you expect us to believe? Even
5 years down the line, if you don't reach that number, we are just supposed to wait?" — the target was
not re-affirmed, re-dated or withdrawn on this call.
3. Management's own admission that the AI thesis was mistimed: "yes, we were wrong in terms of thinking
that AI adoption in such large financial enterprises will become much cleaner, faster… So to that extent,
of course, we were wrong, that the rate of adoption for large enterprises have been slow" and "maybe we
were slightly ahead of our time in terms of our approach to apply AI."
4. Middle East macro risk is now a stated reason to redeploy — "This year, we will pick up U.S. because
of the macroeconomic risk in Middle East" — after Middle East was FY26's growth engine.
5. Security / regulatory operating risk, raised by a shareholder who is an ex-banker: "I've been a
banker for many years and have seen a lot of banks, payment banks, Fintechs completely come undone either
because they clouded the regulatory license or they have not kept pace with technology." Management:
"this exposure that comes in is about a small vulnerability in a piece of software, which was not patched,
which was not even known, that risk is now becoming significantly more and something that we have to keep
on reviewing" — plus DPDP and data-security compliance load. No risk-management slide exists; the
shareholder asked for one.
6. No AI disclosure framework. "someone might see CCAvenue as a payment company that talks about AI" —
management conceded the point ("That's a good suggestion. We'll take that up.") but committed to no
metric and no date.
7. Disclosure opacity generally — no EBITDA, no cash/debt, no TPV number, no segment P&L, no Rediff
financials, no capex, undefined "adjusted" PAT. For a company whose stated growth is +103%, the
verifiable disclosure surface on this call is thin.
8. Enterprise AI adoption cycle risk is unresolved by management's own account: "the cost of tokens has
also been — some people say it's higher, some people say it's lower."
9. Rediff IPO information vacuum — quantum, timing and use of proceeds all withheld; consolidated-margin
impact of Rediff's post-IPO spend was asked and not answered with numbers.
10. Call logistics: the CMD dropped off mid-answer while answering the Rediff capex question
("I think we lost Vishal"), and the Rediff investment/margin question was never fully answered.
management quality / tone: Candour where it is uncomfortable — the strongest positive signal on the call. Twice, unprompted by any
softening: "we were wrong." Vishwas Patel added the industry-level cover — "This is universal, not just
specific to us, actually. So AI adoption is slow" — but the admission itself was Vishal Mehta's and was
not walked back.
Deliberately damping expectations rather than selling the +103%: "we don't see a hockey stick in FY '27
in profitability." A management team optimising for the print would not lead with that.
Heavy strategic abstraction. The opening remarks run several pages of "convergence," "orchestration
layers," "compounding ecosystem advantage," "AI-native commerce and Agentic financial ecosystems" with
almost no numbers attached. Vision-to-metric ratio on this call is very high.
Defensive posture on the two hardest questions. XDuce governance was answered by disowning control
("We don't participate in the Board… we don't allocate the funds"), and the missed 30% international
target was answered with a macro essay on enterprise AI adoption rather than a re-dated commitment.
Receptive to disclosure suggestions, non-committal on delivery. Both the AI-metrics slide and the Rediff
segment split were met with "That's a good suggestion. We'll take that up." / "Absolutely. Thanks." —
no timeline attached to either.
Genuine technical depth where it exists. The agent-to-agent payment architecture, custodianship,
guardrails, kill-switch and MCP answer was specific, unscripted and internally consistent — this is the one
part of the AI narrative that reads as built rather than briefed.
non-obvious takeaways: 1. The company renamed itself before the business changed. Infibeam Avenues → AvenuesAI Limited, and
the transcript still carries the analyst's instinct ("So the Infibeam Board would have probably given
approval…"). The AI revenue that justifies the name is, by management's own words, "not material" to
the P&L today. The rename is a statement of intent, not of mix.
2. The headline growth number is the least informative number on the call. +103% gross vs +15% net. Anyone
quoting ₹8,116cr as revenue growth is quoting merchant TPV pass-through.
3. They are buying access, not assets. 2.5% of Ratnaafin buys no earnings — it buys the right to plug an
NBFC balance sheet into their merchant funnel. Expect a series of such sub-5% stakes ("more than one
NBFC"), which will be near-invisible in consolidated financials while materially changing the business
model. Watch related-party and investment schedules, not the P&L.
4. The high-margin business is the one that stopped growing. Platform/e-commerce is flat; payments — the
thin-margin line — is doing all the volume work. That is the inverse of the mix a fintech re-rating needs.
5. CCAvenue is quietly becoming vertical SaaS. A central reservation system for 3,000+ hotels certified on
Opera/Micros-Fidelio is hospitality software with a gateway attached, not a gateway. It puts them adjacent
to travel/hospitality SaaS names rather than to wallets.
6. A listed-company read-through arrived through the back door. XDuce — 20%-owned by AvenuesAI — put
~₹12cr into DEV Information Technologies (DEVIT · 543462), disclosed by an analyst, not by
management, and management declined responsibility for it.
7. Two-factor authentication is being used as the strategic answer to agentic-payment risk — "a payment
agent cannot execute the command without the customer finally going and saying that, yes, I'm going to
verify." India's 2FA mandate is being reframed from a conversion tax into a moat against autonomous-agent
fraud, and the same mandate is why "the fraud rates are pretty low."
8. Management named its own capital-allocation heuristic: "where we think that we have lighted a small
fire, we pour gasoline on it until it becomes larger." That explains the abrupt Middle East → US pivot and
predicts future abruptness.
9. What they claim NOT to want is as telling as what they want: no balance sheet, no compute, no
subsidiary-led growth, no board seats at XDuce, no take-rate optimisation. The strategy is defined largely
by refusals.
10. The most valuable disclosure on the call was a negative one: FY27 guidance deferred to the Q1 call.
Anyone acting on this note's guidance section without the Q1 FY27 update is acting on a placeholder.

Profitability — actively damped: "we don't see a hockey stick in FY '27 in profitability" and
"it's reasonable to assume that it will be similar to what we have seen in the past years FY '27 should
be." Operating leverage conceded only "in pockets".
Margin: "in terms of consolidated basis, we should continue seeing similar numbers or maybe slightly
higher" — against an acknowledged headwind: "we are in the payment gateway business is somewhat — there
is margin pressure."
Take rates — deliberately not optimised: "our focus remains on building long-term ecosystem value
rather than optimizing for short-term take rates", but also "We'll work very hard in terms of ensuring
that we are able to get our take rates better, and that will require quite a bit of work and optimization."
Capex / commissioning dates: refused. "in terms of the capex, we have certain guidelines and
policies that we are not able to share a lot of information about, specifics on Rediff." No capex number,
no NBFC-investment quantum beyond the 2.5% Ratnaafin stake, no commissioning dates of any kind.
Platform segment: "you will see a lot more activities on the platform side in FY '27" and
"you'll see some amount of growth in that business" — undated, unquantified.
AI revenue: "We do have specific AI revenue as well, which from a size of the P&L is not material" →
"as and when it becomes large enough that we'd want to talk about it, and you'll hear more and more of
that in this year from us."
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business; no backlog, inflow or pipeline metric is reported. The nearest equivalents
disclosed on the call are merchant-acquisition proxies, all volume-based and unmonetised in the disclosure:
Form builder: "more than 5,000 merchants were onboarded on the form builder in less than a month" —
serving "a lot of education institutions, a lot of small merchants, a lot of event merchants."
Hospitality vertical: "now we're scaling up to more than 3,000 hotels, where we're building the entire
central reservation system along with the payment gateway built in" — certified with Opera and
Micros-Fidelio, "which is used by almost all the 5-stars and some of the bigger 4-star chains",
integrating to GDS/PMS so bookings from "any OTA like Booking.com or Expedia or MakeMyTrip" settle
automatically.
Q4 merchant wins: "there has been a good merchant wins that we have had in this last Q4 quarter, which
has translated into good growth of TPV"; strength in "utility, government payments, B2B payments."
Share-of-wallet capture (a cost, admitted): "merchants will be using multiple payment options —
payment gateway options. And we have been very consciously going after the merchants to move processing
volumes to us. It comes at a cost, but I think it's one worth making."
segment / subsidiary detail: Payments — CCAvenue (the engine). Enterprise merchant acquiring across enterprises, SMEs, education,
travel, telecom, government and digital commerce. Growth driver stated as platform-plus-payments, not
gateway pricing: "you put up a platform layer over a payments layer, so it becomes a big hook for bigger
merchants to stay on and increase volumes… It's just another vanilla payment gateway. So it's a platform
plus payments play that has come."
Platform / e-commerce software — flat, and it is the high-margin line. The analyst framing was
"your e-commerce platform is kind of degrowing… that's a high-margin business for us." Management
corrected the direction but not the substance: "the platform business is slightly flat to slightly
higher… the full year numbers in the segment there, you'll see that they are somewhat flat to slightly
higher." Fix proposed is FY27 product rebuild + international.
Rediff / RediffOne / RediffPay — being repositioned from media to fintech. "Historically, Rediff was
viewed primarily as an Internet media and communication platform. We increasingly see it becoming a
broader consumer engagement and financial participation layer", expanding "into areas including payments,
financial engagement, wealth, participation in brokerage, consumer commerce." RediffPay is a
consumer-facing UPI app — "It's actually live and in production", currently being stabilised then
scaled. Today "most of the business is B2B." Rediff has filed a confidential DRHP — "Given the
regulatory compliances, we are not able to share anything additional at this time."
XDuce (US, 20% associate). Taken 2024, $10 million for 20% — "we have not acquired. We've taken
20% in XDuce." Profitable: "they have been a profitable company. They make a few million dollars every
year." Governance stance stated flatly: "We don't participate in the Board of XDuce and we don't allocate
the funds. They have their own control mechanism." (See §10 — this was the sharpest exchange on the call.)
International. FY26 focus was Middle East + GIFT City. FY27 pivots to the US: "This year, we will pick
up U.S. because of the macroeconomic risk in Middle East" — and the internal doctrine, verbatim:
"where we think that we have lighted a small fire, we pour gasoline on it until it becomes larger."
Embedded finance / NBFC stakes. "We are not going to put our balance sheet for lending… What we will
do selectively is to invest minority stakes in more than one NBFC." First is Ratnaafin — "up to
2.5%". Screen for further stakes: "NBFCs with a few thousand crores of AUM, which have a good operating
history, which have scale, which are next generation and well-run management." Plus the Online PSB
Loans proposed strategic investment — "potentially connects us to one of India's most important digital
lending infrastructure backed by major financial institutions."
AI stack. IAIRO (India AI Research Organization) participation, CommerceAI, PayCentral, agent
frameworks across "transaction routing, merchant operations, fraud management, reconciliation, compliance,
automation and customer engagement."
growth verticals / optionality: Agentic payments — the most concrete new capability described. "we have bit of payment agents as well,
just to let you know." Architecture given end-to-end: a discovery agent finds the option, customer
intent converts it to a command, then "that execution will go from discovery agent to a payment agent. So
there will be an agent to agent protocol transfer that happens. And that payment agent is actually
going to go again to AvenuesAI's payment framework, whether it's through MCP… or it will go directly
into executing that if the merchant is integrated using CCAvenue." Two-factor auth remains the human gate.
Embedded merchant lending — merchant financing, checkout financing, working capital, consumer
financing, AI-assisted underwriting, distributed through NBFC partners, no own balance sheet.
Rediff IPO — confidential DRHP filed; an analyst explicitly raised the SOTP angle: "maybe there
will be an SOPP kind of valuation, which might emerge if and when we get Rediff listed."
Sovereign-data-stack pull — "given the macroeconomics of data, data privacy and sovereignty of data,
there's a lot of incentives for very large institutions and merchants to move to a sovereign stack… we
believe it becomes a very large opportunity in '27 and '28."
US cross-border acquiring — "cross-border commerce, global merchant acquiring international
settlements and AI-native payment orchestration represents a large underpenetrated opportunity."
Direct AI revenue — exists, "from a size of the P&L is not material", framed as future optionality.
6a. moat & competitive position: Workflow lock-in beats gateway pricing — evidenced with named certifications. The hospitality build is
a full central reservation system certified with Opera / Micros-Fidelio, integrated to GDS and property
management systems so that "when reservation comes in through, say, any OTA like Booking.com or Expedia or
MakeMyTrip, it gets automated systems and payments are collected automatically." Management's own
conclusion: "those workloads customization is where we are winning, putting a platform with a payments
play. That's where the real growth for us is coming." Scale evidence: 3,000+ hotels.
Distribution velocity on self-serve tooling: "more than 5,000 merchants were onboarded on the form
builder in less than a month."
Data/intelligence compounding — asserted, not yet evidenced with a metric: "The more transactions we
process, the more intelligent the platform accumulates… the stronger the long-term defensibility of the
platform." Recorded as management's stated moat thesis; no supporting number was offered, so treat as
claim rather than demonstrated moat.
Where they explicitly disclaim a moat: compute. "we don't have a very large role to play in compute
because we're not a chip design firm, we don't manufacture chips and we are not going that route. So we
just think that we have to work on algos and data."
margins & cost dynamics: Core gateway margin is under pressure, stated plainly: "We are in the payment gateway business is
somewhat — there is margin pressure."
Costs are front-loaded and deliberate: "Quite a few of other costs are front loaded, specifically some
of the investments that we're making in the AI setup and also, the opportunities that are there in front of
us."
Operating leverage is partial: "in pockets, we are seeing the operating leverage kicking in with
scale", aided by "the productivity that we are getting through this optimization and productivity gains
from AI are also not insignificant."
Winning share costs money: moving merchant volume off competing gateways "comes at a cost."
The mix problem: the high-margin platform line is flat while the low-margin gross-payment line more than
doubled — mathematically a mix headwind to the net-revenue margin, even though management guides
consolidated margin to "similar numbers or maybe slightly higher."
AI is a cost today, revenue tomorrow: direct AI revenue is "not material" to the P&L while AI
infrastructure spend is explicitly part of the front-loaded cost base.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): No capex number was given, and the refusal was explicit when asked directly for capex guidance across
NBFC investments, infrastructure and Rediff: "in terms of the capex, we have certain guidelines and
policies that we are not able to share a lot of information about, specifics on Rediff."
Capex philosophy, in their framing: "more at a capex level, we look at three things, which is in the
world of AI, genuinely, we think there's only compute, algos and data" — with compute explicitly
excluded from their remit.
Committed / announced deployments (amounts mostly undisclosed): Ratnaafin NBFC minority up to 2.5%;
Online PSB Loans proposed strategic investment (quantum not disclosed); XDuce $10mn for 20% (2024,
historic); Rediff platform investment (quantum withheld); US market build-out (undated, unquantified);
AI infrastructure (part of the front-loaded cost base, unquantified).
Discipline claim: "Our strategy is not subsidiary-led growth. Our strategy is infrastructure-led,
intelligence-led and ecosystem-led growth."
⚠️ Slippage watch: the US expansion is itself an admitted slip — the 30% international revenue
target was set in February 2024 and, per the analyst and undisputed by management, "as of now, also, we
are not close to that number." Track the US build and the international mix against that original target.
capital allocation: Explicit refusal to become a lender: "We are not going to put our balance sheet for lending."
Restated by Vishwas Patel: "our strategy remains asset-light and scalable. We are not looking to become a
traditional balance sheet lender."
Chosen instrument: repeated small minority stakes in NBFCs, deliberately more than one —
"invest minority stakes in more than one NBFC"; Ratnaafin is "the first one that we've opened up, where
we've taken up, up to 2.5%." Rationale is ecosystem access, not returns on the stake: "we are able to
connect our ecosystem very tightly with such NBFCs… and we would allow the NBFCs to continue opening up the
lending opportunities to our merchant and merchant ecosystem and consumer ecosystems."
Online PSB Loans — proposed strategic investment announced on the call day, positioned as access to
"one of India's most important digital lending infrastructure backed by major financial institutions."
Rediff monetisation via IPO — confidential DRHP filed; details withheld under regulatory silence.
XDuce — capital allocated, control expressly not retained. This is the governance question of the call
(§10): AvenuesAI put $10mn into a 20% stake and states "We don't participate in the Board of XDuce and we
don't allocate the funds."
No dividend, buyback, debt-reduction, promoter-pledge or fund-raise discussion occurred on this call.
risks & watch-items: 1. The XDuce capital-deployment challenge — the sharpest exchange on the call. Analyst Ayushi:
"when we acquired XDuce, the Board had stated two specific objectives. One was that we were embedding
Phronetic AI into XDuce's framework, and then second was growing CCAvenue's U.S. payment business. So
since that investment, XDuce has made at least two significant capital deployments that are entirely
unrelated to those objectives" — specifically "one investment in a U.S. cybersecurity firm and the other
investment in DEV Information Technologies, which is an Indian listed company… they have spent around
INR12 crores in that particular transaction." Management's reply was a governance disclaimer, not a
rebuttal on substance: "I think that's an incorrect statement. We don't participate in the Board of XDuce
and we don't allocate the funds." Watch: whether the two stated XDuce objectives are ever delivered.
2. A multi-year target publicly missed. "the 30% target for international revenue was made in February
2024. Sir, as of now, also, we are not close to that number. So what do you expect us to believe? Even
5 years down the line, if you don't reach that number, we are just supposed to wait?" — the target was
not re-affirmed, re-dated or withdrawn on this call.
3. Management's own admission that the AI thesis was mistimed: "yes, we were wrong in terms of thinking
that AI adoption in such large financial enterprises will become much cleaner, faster… So to that extent,
of course, we were wrong, that the rate of adoption for large enterprises have been slow" and "maybe we
were slightly ahead of our time in terms of our approach to apply AI."
4. Middle East macro risk is now a stated reason to redeploy — "This year, we will pick up U.S. because
of the macroeconomic risk in Middle East" — after Middle East was FY26's growth engine.
5. Security / regulatory operating risk, raised by a shareholder who is an ex-banker: "I've been a
banker for many years and have seen a lot of banks, payment banks, Fintechs completely come undone either
because they clouded the regulatory license or they have not kept pace with technology." Management:
"this exposure that comes in is about a small vulnerability in a piece of software, which was not patched,
which was not even known, that risk is now becoming significantly more and something that we have to keep
on reviewing" — plus DPDP and data-security compliance load. No risk-management slide exists; the
shareholder asked for one.
6. No AI disclosure framework. "someone might see CCAvenue as a payment company that talks about AI" —
management conceded the point ("That's a good suggestion. We'll take that up.") but committed to no
metric and no date.
7. Disclosure opacity generally — no EBITDA, no cash/debt, no TPV number, no segment P&L, no Rediff
financials, no capex, undefined "adjusted" PAT. For a company whose stated growth is +103%, the
verifiable disclosure surface on this call is thin.
8. Enterprise AI adoption cycle risk is unresolved by management's own account: "the cost of tokens has
also been — some people say it's higher, some people say it's lower."
9. Rediff IPO information vacuum — quantum, timing and use of proceeds all withheld; consolidated-margin
impact of Rediff's post-IPO spend was asked and not answered with numbers.
10. Call logistics: the CMD dropped off mid-answer while answering the Rediff capex question
("I think we lost Vishal"), and the Rediff investment/margin question was never fully answered.
management quality / tone: Candour where it is uncomfortable — the strongest positive signal on the call. Twice, unprompted by any
softening: "we were wrong." Vishwas Patel added the industry-level cover — "This is universal, not just
specific to us, actually. So AI adoption is slow" — but the admission itself was Vishal Mehta's and was
not walked back.
Deliberately damping expectations rather than selling the +103%: "we don't see a hockey stick in FY '27
in profitability." A management team optimising for the print would not lead with that.
Heavy strategic abstraction. The opening remarks run several pages of "convergence," "orchestration
layers," "compounding ecosystem advantage," "AI-native commerce and Agentic financial ecosystems" with
almost no numbers attached. Vision-to-metric ratio on this call is very high.
Defensive posture on the two hardest questions. XDuce governance was answered by disowning control
("We don't participate in the Board… we don't allocate the funds"), and the missed 30% international
target was answered with a macro essay on enterprise AI adoption rather than a re-dated commitment.
Receptive to disclosure suggestions, non-committal on delivery. Both the AI-metrics slide and the Rediff
segment split were met with "That's a good suggestion. We'll take that up." / "Absolutely. Thanks." —
no timeline attached to either.
Genuine technical depth where it exists. The agent-to-agent payment architecture, custodianship,
guardrails, kill-switch and MCP answer was specific, unscripted and internally consistent — this is the one
part of the AI narrative that reads as built rather than briefed.
non-obvious takeaways: 1. The company renamed itself before the business changed. Infibeam Avenues → AvenuesAI Limited, and
the transcript still carries the analyst's instinct ("So the Infibeam Board would have probably given
approval…"). The AI revenue that justifies the name is, by management's own words, "not material" to
the P&L today. The rename is a statement of intent, not of mix.
2. The headline growth number is the least informative number on the call. +103% gross vs +15% net. Anyone
quoting ₹8,116cr as revenue growth is quoting merchant TPV pass-through.
3. They are buying access, not assets. 2.5% of Ratnaafin buys no earnings — it buys the right to plug an
NBFC balance sheet into their merchant funnel. Expect a series of such sub-5% stakes ("more than one
NBFC"), which will be near-invisible in consolidated financials while materially changing the business
model. Watch related-party and investment schedules, not the P&L.
4. The high-margin business is the one that stopped growing. Platform/e-commerce is flat; payments — the
thin-margin line — is doing all the volume work. That is the inverse of the mix a fintech re-rating needs.
5. CCAvenue is quietly becoming vertical SaaS. A central reservation system for 3,000+ hotels certified on
Opera/Micros-Fidelio is hospitality software with a gateway attached, not a gateway. It puts them adjacent
to travel/hospitality SaaS names rather than to wallets.
6. A listed-company read-through arrived through the back door. XDuce — 20%-owned by AvenuesAI — put
~₹12cr into DEV Information Technologies (DEVIT · 543462), disclosed by an analyst, not by
management, and management declined responsibility for it.
7. Two-factor authentication is being used as the strategic answer to agentic-payment risk — "a payment
agent cannot execute the command without the customer finally going and saying that, yes, I'm going to
verify." India's 2FA mandate is being reframed from a conversion tax into a moat against autonomous-agent
fraud, and the same mandate is why "the fraud rates are pretty low."
8. Management named its own capital-allocation heuristic: "where we think that we have lighted a small
fire, we pour gasoline on it until it becomes larger." That explains the abrupt Middle East → US pivot and
predicts future abruptness.
9. What they claim NOT to want is as telling as what they want: no balance sheet, no compute, no
subsidiary-led growth, no board seats at XDuce, no take-rate optimisation. The strategy is defined largely
by refusals.
10. The most valuable disclosure on the call was a negative one: FY27 guidance deferred to the Q1 call.
Anyone acting on this note's guidance section without the Q1 FY27 update is acting on a placeholder.

hero.oneLiner:
AvenuesAI (ex-Infibeam Avenues) re-badged itself this quarter from a payment gateway into an "AI-first
financial infrastructure and transaction intelligence platform," and FY26 headline growth is spectacular
only at the gross line — revenue from operations **+103% to ₹8,116cr** while **net revenue rose just +15%
to ₹603cr**, i.e. the growth is TPV pass-through, not monetisation. The real Q4 news is strategic, not
financial: a declared asset-light pivot into embedded lending via **minority NBFC stakes** (Ratnaafin, up to
2.5%) and a **proposed strategic investment in Online PSB Loans announced on the call day**, plus a
**confidential DRHP filed for Rediff**. Management explicitly withheld FY27 guidance ("we'll give guidance in
the first quarter call for the full year"), pre-empted a profit re-rating ("we don't see a hockey stick in
FY '27 in profitability"), and — unusually — conceded its prior AI/US thesis was mistimed: "yes, we were
wrong in terms of thinking that AI adoption in such large financial enterprises will become much cleaner,
faster."
